brief: SEB's Nordic morning note leads with one causal chain: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO after admitting a relationship with a suspected Chinese spy, and that shock, combined with higher Brent oil prices and rising interest rates, drove risk-off flows that pulled US equities down (S&P 500 and Nasdaq both -0.4%) while European stocks diverged higher (Euro Stoxx 50 +0.1%); the euro weakened against the dollar and gold fell; Asian markets opened mixed, up in Japan, down in China. Beyond that chain the note only reports, without arguing further: Trump said the US does not need an Iran deal and told Vance to pursue corruption in opposition-controlled districts; Trump threatened to double Mexico tariffs over roughly 1,500 migrants heading to the border; Zelenskyy said Starshield access for Ukraine's military has again been curtailed, hurting drone defense; a 25bp Peru rate hike is expected; and a calendar of European/EM data, central bank speeches and credit-rating reviews is due. Nordic section: the krona weakened, OMX30 closed flat, and Sweden's Center Party set a same-day deadline for rival leaders' coalition proposals.
